newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hughes's Armstrong says no talks on AT&T post.
newsitem.headline: Hughes's Armstrong says no talks on AT&T post.

text.p: Michael armstrong, chairman and chief executive of Hughes Electronics Corp, told Reuters on Wednesday that he has not talked with AT&T about becoming president of the U.S. long-distance carrier.
"It is not true that I am in discussions with AT&T. I haven't been contacted by the company and I have not been offered the job," Armstrong said in an interview.
"I am very happy and intend to stay with Hughes," he said. "You have to ask AT&T who they are considering."
Asked if he would take the job if it was offered, he said: "I haven't the faintest idea."

There has been media speculation in the United States that Armstrong would be picked to replace Alex Mandle, who resigned two months ago. The reports also said the new president was likely to be announced this week.

Armstrong, who left for the United States later on Wednesday, was in Tokyo to announce that DirecTV Japan Inc, a group company of Hughes Electronics Corp, would start a digital satellite broadcasting service in Japan in autumn 1997.

DirecTV will become the third digital satellite broadcasting company to start broadcasting in Japan after PerfecTV, which is owned by a consortium headed by trading company Itochu Corp, and J-SkyB, which is due to be launched next April.
J-SkyB is a venture between Australian media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and Japan's Softbank Corp .
PerfecTV launched its service earlier this month.
